questions.title: Which city will be the site of Typhoon Dolphin's first landfall in mainland China in August 2026?
questions.background: Dolphin developed into a typhoon over the Pacific in late July 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Landfall information issued by China's meteorological authorities, either directly or through contemporaneous reliable news coverage. This significantly shifts and broadens probability mass northward relative to yesterday's Zhejiang-Fujian border concentration: cutting Wenzhou (0.23 -> 0.17) and Ningde (0.20 -> 0.14), holding Taizhou (0.16, central Zhejiang bullseye), lifting Ningbo (0.11 -> 0.13, absorbing mainland follow-through from excluded Zhoushan offshore islands; Ningbo/Wenzhou/Zhoushan/Taizhou issued defense notices today per CZTV), and bringing Shanghai into #5 (0.11, replacing Fuzhou 0.08) as the unique Yangtze River mouth hinge city explicitly named in both CMA scenarios. local_articles.title: Typhoon Dolphin hurtles towards Japan: Tracker, updates and what to expect
local_articles.snippet: Typhoon Dolphin is heading westwards across the Pacific Ocean towards Japan, and residents of Okinawa Island have been urged to prepare for severe weather before its expected landfall this week. Dolphin has taken a long voyage across the ocean, and as it approaches Japan, here’s what to expect in the coming days. How strong is Typhoon Dolphin? According to Zoom Earth, Dolphin is a “very strong typhoon” that was moving at 185 kilometres per hour (115 miles per hour) at 05:00 GMT on Tuesday. It grew out of a tropical depression that emerged on July 26, moving at 45km/h (30mph) over the open waters of the Central Pacific Ocean as it embarked on a journey of several thousand kilometres across the Pacific. questions.title: Who will be appointed to succeed Pape Thiaw as head coach of Senegal's men's national football team by August 31, 2026?
questions.background: The Senegalese Football Federation is responsible for appointing the national team's head coach.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official announcement by the Senegalese Football Federation, as confirmed by contemporaneous reliable news reporting. Resolution : Resolve to the person publicly announced as Pape Thiaw's successor between August 1 and August 31, 2026. The resolution date is the date the appointment is publicly announced, rather than the coach's presentation or first match. Accepted Answer Format : The appointed coach's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major double update since June 24: first, Senegal officially fired Pape Thiaw on July 11 (Al Jazeera/Straits Times) after losing World Cup group games to France and Norway and blowing a 2-0 lead in a 3-2 AET Round of 32 loss to Belgium. Second, Tier-1 French daily L'Équipe reported on Saturday July 25 (via Goal.com) that the race has narrowed primarily to Dakar-born Patrick Vieira and two-time AFCON champion Hervé Renard, with Vieira leading the race, talks at an advanced stage, and initial approval given by Vieira (free agent since leaving Genoa in Nov 2025; strong FSF support via Senegalese roots and Diambars academy). However, L'Équipe notes the appointment is held up by Senegalese political friction between President Bassirou Diomaye Faye and ex-PM Ousmane Sonko, formal termination of Thiaw's contract, and Ministry of Sport approval (explaining why announcement slips into the Aug 1-31 window). Respecting anti-overconfidence on unconfirmed talks and ministerial veto risk, place Patrick Vieira at 0.42, Hervé Renard at 0.23 (explicit #2 finalist after brief Tunisia WC stint), Omar Daf at 0.12 (leading local/FSF-favored Senegalese option reported July 13; prime fallback if politics/salary block Vieira/Renard), Habib Beye at 0.07 (cited in July 13-15 four-man pool), and Malick Daf at 0.02 (internal FSF youth fallback), leaving 0.14 for surprise candidates.

questions.title: Which major US employment sector will shed the most jobs in July 2026?
questions.background: The US Bureau of Labor Statistics reports monthly changes in nonfarm payroll employment by sector.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the broad employment sector with the largest net decline in payroll jobs in July 2026, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics' initial employment report for that month, released in August 2026. Resolution Date : 2026-08-07 Accepted Answer Format : Compare sectors by the number of jobs lost, not percentage changes, and count subsectors within their parent sectors. Answer with the sector's name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-31 to 2026-08-03 macro and labor updates ahead of the Aug 7 BLS July jobs report (consensus +83k Reuters / +87.5k FactSet / +100k KPMG / +63k RBC): (1) Today's ISM Manufacturing PMI (Aug 3, Reuters/Straits Times) surged to a 4-year high of 55.6 (vs 53.3 June, 54.0 est) and critically the ISM Manufacturing Employment index rebounded sharply into expansion at 52.8 (highest since Aug 2022, up from 49.7), while KPMG (July 31) projects net manufacturing gains — sharply lowering Manufacturing's odds of being the top loser (0.15 -> ~0.08 in residual, retaining only July auto-retooling shutdown variance flagged by KPMG and RBC). (2) Leisure and hospitality rises #1 (0.18 -> 0.21): RBC (July 31) explicitly forecasts continued losses following June's -54.6k drop as the World Cup ends, and KPMG warns a late-July wave of Haitian TPS expirations hit leisure and hospitality payrolls disproportionately (without showing up in jobless claims) alongside weak discretionary dining. (3) Financial activities climbs to #2 (0.15 -> 0.18) as RBC highlights ongoing service-sector job losses concentrated in finance and information, citing persistent residential real estate (-34k since end-2023) and mortgage brokering (-45k) cuts amid rising mortgage rates. (4) Government trims slightly (0.17 -> 0.15) with KPMG expecting +5k public payrolls and MNI seeing flat public payrolls as federal reductions stabilize, though huge 23M base and July state/local education seasonal-adjustment swings keep it top-3. (5) Trade, transportation, and utilities holds at 0.14 (29M base, RBC sees minimal/flat gains under tariff drag). (6) Information enters #5 at 0.10 (replacing Manufacturing): RBC explicitly names Information alongside Finance as where service losses are concentrated, and in a +83k to +100k rebound month a steady contraction in Information can top the net-decline chart despite its smaller 3M base. Top-5 sum 0.78 leaves 22% residual across Manufacturing (~0.08), Professional and business services (~0.06, KPMG expects gains), Construction (~0.04), Other services (~0.02), Mining and logging (~0.01), and Private education and health services (~0.01).
